subject: Availability windowing and service-credit formula — RFI follow-up
messages:
From: Sally Park <sally.park@nebula-enterprises.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nebula-enterprises.com
Date: 2028-04-01T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Question on availability windowing + credits (Nebula RFI)

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the RFI submission — our procurement team is working through the availability / credit sections and has two specific asks before we complete the scorecard: 1) how you define "downtime windows" when only a portion of our traffic (cross-region or regional failover) is affected, and 2) the exact math you use to translate measured outage minutes into monetary credits.

We received a CSV of your telemetry samples but need the formula you apply so our SREs can run a quick validation. Can you provide a short worked example (with numbers) and clarify whether synthetic probe failures are treated differently from customer request sampling?

Appreciate a quick reply — we have an internal deadline Friday (2028-04-05).

Best,
Sally
Sally Park
Senior Procurement Manager
Nebula Enterprises
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sally Park <sally.park@nebula-enterprises.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, procurement@nebula-enterprises.com
Date: 2028-04-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on availability windowing + credits (Nebula RFI)

Hi Sally — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching a worked example (spreadsheet) and a short explanation below. If anything is unclear we can hop on a 30m call.

Summary (short):
- Windowing: we compute availability per-region per-hour using sampled customer request telemetry; a region is considered degraded for a given UTC hour if the measured successful request ratio falls below the committed availability threshold for that hour. Multi-region weighting is applied at the customer-configured traffic distribution at the time of the incident (we use weighted availability).
- Partial degradations: credits are pro-rated based on the fraction of customer traffic that experienced degraded availability during the affected window.
- Conversion to credits: outage_minutes -> degraded_windows -> credit % using a tiered matrix. Math below.

Worked example (numbers):
- Contract: 99.95% monthly availability (for simplicity assume 30-day month = 43,200 minutes).
- Measured: between 2028-03-15 03:00Z and 2028-03-15 05:00Z, a subset of traffic routed to us (Region A) experienced elevated error rates. Region A handles 40% of customer traffic at the time.
- In that 2-hour period (120 minutes) the successful request ratio in Region A dropped to 98.5% for both covered hours; other regions were within SLA. For our calculation we count both hours as degraded windows.

Step 1 — Determine degraded minutes attributable to customer traffic: 120 minutes * 0.40 = 48 degraded customer-minutes.
Step 2 — Convert to monthly availability delta: (48 / 43200) * 100 = 0.111% availability loss.
Step 3 — Apply credit matrix (example matrix in attached spreadsheet): for 0.05% - 0.2% loss -> 5% service credit on monthly invoice.

Key notes:
- We prefer to use customer-request sampling for primary attribution (sampling of successful/error responses). Synthetic probes are used as a secondary signal for early detection and to help adjudicate, but primary crediting is based on production request telemetry unless customers opt-in to a probe-only SLA.
- When traffic shifts mid-window we re-weight the window by observed traffic distribution during that hour; we do not apply a simple per-region boolean unless explicitly requested in the contract.

I've attached: 1) redwood-service-credit-matrix-v1.xlsx (credit tiers + examples), 2) a CSV of sampled telemetry windows (nebularfi_telemetry_samples.csv).

If you want a simpler conservative option (treat full-region degradation as full traffic impact), we can supply that as an alternative crediting model for procurement teams who prefer simpler arithmetic.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Sally Park <sally.park@nebula-enterprises.com>

Date: 2028-04-01T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on availability windowing + credits (Nebula RFI)

Sally/Naomi — quick clarification from our end on sampling and burst windows:
- Sampling cadence: production request sampling is at 1:500 for telemetry rows in the CSV; when sampling density yields fewer than 30 sampled requests in a given hour we switch to a conservative aggregation (treat as potentially degraded and combine neighboring hours) and flag for manual review.
- Burst windows: we apply a 5-minute smoothing window to avoid single-minute noise triggering a full-hour degradation. The rule is: an hourly window is marked degraded if the >5 minute rolling median success ratio for the hour is below threshold for at least 40% of the hour.
- Cross-region weighting: we compute weighted availability using observed session affinity where available; otherwise we use egress distribution averaged over the hour.

If Nebula's SREs want the raw sampling algorithm we can share pseudocode. Also looping in Lauren for any procurement/legal constraints on making the conservative option the default.

-Karthik
Head of Runtime Reliability
Redwood Inference

Thanks Naomi/Karthik — the worked example helps. Two follow-ups from our SRE and Finance teams: 1) can you confirm the maximum time to adjudicate and issue a credit (we have language that requires credits to be issued within 30 days of incident close), and 2) for multi-region customers, can you provide an example where traffic shifts mid-hour (you mentioned re-weighting) — we want to understand if re-weighting could reduce a credit by more than 50% in a realistic worst-case.

Also, are your synthetic probe results visible to customers in the same telemetry dump or are they separated? Our SREs prefer to see probe traces alongside sampled requests for their validation process.

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Question on availability windowing + credits (Nebula RFI)

Tim/Sally — answers inline and next steps: 

1) Credit issuance SLA: we commit to a 45-day window to complete investigation and apply a service credit after incident close by default. We can tighten to 30 days with an enterprise addendum (we have customers on both 30 and 45 day timelines; legal will need to sign).

2) Mid-hour re-weighting example (conservative worst-case):
- Hour H: first 30 minutes traffic distribution A=70%, B=30%. Next 30 minutes distribution A=20%, B=80% (major client shift). If only Region A degrades for whole hour, weighted degraded-minutes = (30min * 0.70) + (30min * 0.20) = 27 degraded minutes out of 60 -> 45% of the hour effectively degraded. That could reduce the effective credit compared to counting the full hour at 100% traffic (which would be 60 degraded minutes). In short, re-weighting can significantly reduce the dollar credit versus a naive per-region boolean, but the re-weighting reflects actual customer impact.

3) Synthetic probes: we include probes as a separate column in the CSV we share; customers see probe results adjacent to sampled request rows. We annotate rows where probes and request sampling disagree for easier triage.

4) Next steps: per your deadline, we can: A) proceed with the default weighted model above, B) offer an alternative conservative model (full-region-impact) if Nebula procurement prefers simplicity, or C) include both models in the contract and use the conservative one for initial 6-month onboarding. Please indicate a preference and we will provide language for the contract appendix.

I'll open a HubSpot ticket for the procurement/legal flow and share the contract appendix text; Lauren — can you provide the standard 30-day addendum wording if they select the tighter SLA?

Link to tentative appendix draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-nebula-rfi-evidence (see redwood-service-credit-matrix-v1.xlsx). HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-NEBULA-2028-041

Thanks — happy to schedule 30m with your SREs this week to walk through the CSV and sample pseudocode.

Regards,
